outcome: Help financial-crime investigators resolve AML alerts faster by assembling evidence, explaining transaction patterns, and drafting review narratives under human control.
overview: AML investigators lose hours to every alert, switching between monitoring systems, customer records, payment histories, sanctions data and spreadsheets before they can write a single narrative. This solution gives financial-crime teams a governed investigation workspace: it retrieves approved evidence with permissions intact, builds customer and transaction timelines, highlights unusual relationships, answers investigator questions with citations, and drafts case narratives or SAR/STR content for human approval. It augments the bank’s monitoring and filing controls rather than replacing them — every disposition and regulatory filing stays with a human. A proof of value runs in 6–10 weeks, targeting shorter handling times, more consistent case quality and greater investigator capacity.

benefits.text: Cut average alert-investigation time by a target 30–50%
benefits.source: Redington BFSI catalogue; consistent with published AI-assisted investigation case ranges
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target range to validate against the customer’s own handling-time baseline during the PoV — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Increase cases completed per investigator by a target 25% without automatically closing or filing any case
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on evidence-source coverage and disposition quality in the customer’s case history

benefits.text: Show source evidence and access history for every generated statement, cutting QA rework by a target 20%
benefits.source: Reference-design control (mandatory citation and audit logging); Redington BFSI catalogue
benefits.limits: Citation coverage is a platform control; the QA-rework reduction still requires baseline measurement in the pilot

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); regulated case evidence stays in the customer tenancy, with a hybrid-retrieval option where only approved context reaches the model service

notFor.situation: Evidence sources (KYC, transactions, alerts, prior cases) cannot be connected by API or export
notFor.why: The workspace assembles and cites existing evidence; with nothing to retrieve it can only generate unsupported text, which the design forbids

notFor.situation: The goal is automated case closure or automated SAR/STR filing
notFor.why: The solution is deliberately human-in-the-loop — generated content is never filed automatically, so a lights-out operating model is out of scope

notFor.situation: Historical cases lack reliable final dispositions
notFor.why: The PoV benefit case and quality benchmark both compare against confirmed outcomes; without them no honest baseline exists

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer MLRO retains policy and decision ownership throughout · Duration: 6–10 weeks PoV; further 14–24 weeks to production
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, vendor platform specialist; customer MLRO, AML operations owner, data owner, security approver, model-risk/AI-governance reviewer, investigators and QA lead · Support model: Business-hours standard with severity-based response targets; optional extended/24×7 platform support; partner first line with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Workflow and control design
3) Data integration and retrieval build
4) Prompt and template configuration with validation
5) Security test and UAT
6) Training, launch and handover

No decline in QA scores across assisted cases

Human approval enforced end to end; audit logs and monitoring active; trained users sign off
effort: 6–10 weeks PoV; further 14–24 weeks to production
